sections.title: Shamel Backend in its surroundings
sections.question: What sits between the mobile app and Shaheen?

bullets.text: The Mobile API is the only host; the application core and the Shaheen connector are libraries inside it.
Requests for old Shamel routes are forwarded first and never reach the new pipeline.

sections.title: One answer stream, three transports
sections.question: How do HTTP, SSE and SignalR clients get the same answer?

bullets.text: Every transport runs AnswerChannelPump; none has a loop of its own.
The watcher prefers a pushed stream and polls the connector when streaming is not supported.

sections.title: From prompt to answer
sections.question: What happens between a prompt being posted and its answer being read?

bullets.text: Posting a prompt returns 202 with a link; the answer is a separate GET.
Identity comes from the JWT through ToClientContext, never from the request body.

sections.title: Response caching rules
sections.question: Where do the response caching rules come from and how long do they live?

bullets.text: Rules are read from dbo.HeaderCachingConfig, active rows only.
The list is held in a static field and reloaded every 24 hours.
